significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a measurable "coherence gap" between logically linked belief representations predicts subsequent self-contradiction better than statement-level confidence, and that manipulating this geometry causally repairs the contradiction; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) mechanism. It would establish both a phenomenon—contradictions vary with representational alignment across entailments, negations, and chains—and a mechanistic explanation that fixes expectations for unmeasured linked propositions, rather than merely showing that a belief direction exists; this bears directly on the consistency bottleneck studied behaviorally in BeliefBank and related logical-consistency work. A negative result would meaningfully rule out low subspace alignment as a general explanation of belief propagation failures, although it would not distinguish every alternative account, and the true and false states are sufficiently determinate. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on internal LLM beliefs would not retain this score: the specific alignment-to-contradiction coupling and causal propagation account are what raise it above the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "coherence-gap" metric, "internal-contradiction-rate," and a "lightweight propagation intervention" that aligns linked-belief representations. The claim that coherence gaps "predict behavioral self-contradiction" provides potential ex-ante lead time at the query activation, while the repair intervention gives auditors or model developers a possible gating or correction knob rather than only a post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted relation—lower required alignment predicts more contradictions—still predicts what should be found across entailment, negation, transitive-chain, and mutual-exclusion tasks, although the hypothesis does not clearly guarantee invariance across architectures or scales and therefore stops short of very broad deployment reach. The topic-substitution check lowers no score here: research on LLM beliefs alone supplies neither this transferable diagnostic relation nor the propagation handle, but the stated downstream scope remains mainly interpretability and model-auditing practitioners rather than users outside AI.
